statusWithCorrectParams: 200 OK — with ?month=2026-06 (and optional &personId=<uuid>) the endpoint returns a TimeGap[] array. The 500 only occurs when the required `month` query param is missing or malformed.
rootCause: MyTimeController.getGaps reads @Query('month') as a plain string with no validation pipe, then calls parseMonthQuery(monthStr). When `month` is absent, monthStr is undefined and parseMonthQuery does `month.match(...)` -> TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'match'). When `month` is present but malformed (e.g. 2026-13, 'June', empty), parseMonthQuery hits `throw new Error('Invalid month format: ...')`. Both bubble up unhandled and the StructuredExceptionFilter maps them to HTTP 500 instead of 400. A MonthQueryDto with class-validator @Matches exists in the same file (month.query.ts) but is NOT wired into this controller — the raw @Query() string bypasses validation. `personId` is NOT the problem: it is optional (falls back to req.principal.personId) and accepts a raw UUID fine. This route has no path params.

    at parseMonthQuery (/app/dist/src/modules/timesheets/application/contracts/month.query.js:39:25)
    at MyTimeController.getGaps (/app/dist/src/modules/timesheets/presentation/my-time.controller.js:54:67)
    at /app/node_modules/@nestjs/core/router/router-execution-context.js:38:29
    at process.processTicksAndRejections (node:internal/process/task_queues:95:5)
suggestedFix: Wire the existing MonthQueryDto into getGaps (and the sibling getMonth/autoFill/copyPrevious handlers) so the @Matches(/^(\d{4})-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])$/) validator runs and class-validator returns a 400 BadRequest for missing/malformed `month`. Concretely, replace the loose @Query('month') string param with `@Query() q: MonthQueryDto` (global ValidationPipe already present) and read q.month / q.personId. This converts both the undefined-TypeError and the 'Invalid month format' Error paths into proper 400s. Lower priority since the UI never sends a bad month (fetchTimeGaps always builds URLSearchParams({ month })).
uiCaller: frontend/src/lib/api/my-time.ts -> fetchTimeGaps(month, personId?) builds `URLSearchParams({ month })` and only appends personId if truthy — so the UI ALWAYS sends a valid `month` and never triggers the 500. Furthermore fetchTimeGaps is effectively DEAD CODE: no .tsx/.ts (non-test) file imports or calls it. The My Time UI (frontend/src/routes/my-time/MyTimePage.tsx and frontend/src/routes/me/TimeTab.tsx) obtains gaps from the bundled `/my-time/month` response (MonthlyTimesheetResponse.gaps via fetchMonthlyTimesheet), not from the standalone /my-time/gaps endpoint. No real user flow can reach this 500.
